Least-squares means

Source: R/estimates.R
vlm_lsmeans.Rd

Least-squares means (estimated marginal means) of a classification effect of a fitted model, with their standard errors, degrees of freedom and confidence limits, and optionally all pairwise differences with a multiple comparison adjustment: the LSMEANS statement of SAS PROC MIXED.

Usage

vlm_lsmeans(
  fit,
  specs,
  at = NULL,
  diff = FALSE,
  adjust = c("none", "tukey", "bonferroni", "sidak"),
  level = 0.95
)

# Default S3 method
vlm_lsmeans(
  fit,
  specs,
  at = NULL,
  diff = FALSE,
  adjust = c("none", "tukey", "bonferroni", "sidak"),
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

fit

a result of vlm_fit().

specs

the effect: a character string such as "Drug:dose" or a one-sided formula such as ~ Drug:dose (all its variables must be classification variables of the fixed part).

at

optional named list of covariate values (default: the means of the covariates).

diff

logical; also give all pairwise differences (default FALSE).

adjust

multiple comparison adjustment of the differences: "none", "tukey", "bonferroni" or "sidak".

level

confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A list of class c("vlm_lsmeans", "vlm_result", "list") with lsmeans, diffs (NULL unless diff = TRUE) and L (the coefficient rows).

Details

The least-squares mean of a level combination is \(\mathbf{l}^{\top}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}\), where \(\mathbf{l}\) has 1 for the intercept and the matching levels, equal weights \(1/m\) over the \(m\) levels (or cells) of the other factors of each effect, and the mean of each covariate (or the value in at) for covariate columns. Its variance is \(\mathbf{l}^{\top}(\mathbf{X}^{\top} \widehat{\mathbf{V}}^{-1}\mathbf{X})^{-}\mathbf{l}\), the broad-inference-space variance. Non-estimable means are returned as NA. With adjust = "tukey", p-values of the differences come from the studentised range distribution (Tukey-Kramer), \(P(Q_{k,\nu} > \sqrt{2}|t|)\), and the confidence limits use \(q_{k,\nu}(1-\alpha)/\sqrt{2}\).

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi. Sections 2.5.2 and 3.3.

Searle, S. R., Speed, F. M. and Milliken, G. A. (1980). Population marginal means in the linear model: an alternative to least squares means. The American Statistician, 34, 216-221.

See also

vlm_fit, vlm_estimate

Other VetResearchLMM inference: emmeans_mixed_model(), report_mixed_model(), vlm_blup(), vlm_estimate()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
# Example 2.5.2.1: LSMEANS drug*dose
lm1 <-
  vlm_lsmeans(
      fit    = fm
    , specs  = ~ Drug:dose
    , at     = NULL
    , diff   = TRUE
    , adjust = "tukey"
    , level  = 0.95
    )
lm1
